sections.content: The Kerry Blue Terrier is a medium-sized, bold, and intelligent breed known for its distinctive blue coat and lively personality. Originally bred in Ireland for farm work, hunting, and guarding, the Kerry Blue Terrier is a versatile dog with a playful spirit and a deep loyalty to its family. Whether you’re looking for an energetic playmate, a capable watchdog, or a charming show dog, the Kerry Blue Terrier offers both beauty and brains.
Size: Medium Weight: 33-40 lbs Lifespan: 12-15 years Temperament: Spirited, Intelligent, Loyal Coat: Soft, wavy, and dense Exercise Needs: High Group: Terrier

The Kerry Blue Terrier originates from County Kerry, Ireland, where it was developed as an all-purpose farm dog. Known for its versatility, the breed excelled at herding livestock, hunting small game, and even working as a guard dog. Over time, the Kerry Blue also became a favorite in the show ring due to its striking coat and confident presence.
Originated in County Kerry, Ireland . Historically used for herding, hunting, and guarding. Famous for its unique blue coat, which develops over time.
The Kerry Blue Terrier’s signature feature is its dense, wavy coat, which shifts from black at birth to a beautiful shade of blue by adulthood.

Medium-sized, muscular build.  Soft, wavy coat ranging from deep slate to pale silver blue.  Distinctive beard and bushy eyebrows.  Dark, expressive eyes full of intelligence and mischief.  High-set tail carried proudly.
Kerry Blues are spirited, confident, and always ready for action. They form strong bonds with their families and thrive when involved in daily activities.

Loyal and affectionate: Devoted to their family.  Playful and energetic: Always up for fun and games.  Intelligent and curious: Quick learners with a mischievous streak.  Alert and protective: Natural watchdog instincts.
This is a high-energy breed that requires plenty of physical and mental stimulation to stay happy and well-behaved.

1-2 hours of exercise daily, including walks, playtime, and training.  Enjoys agility, obedience, and even advanced tricks training.  Responds well to positive reinforcement , but requires firm, consistent leadership.  Socialization from a young age helps manage the breed’s natural boldness.

sections.section: ️ Grooming and Care of the Kerry Blue Terrier
sections.content: The Kerry Blue’s unique coat requires regular grooming to keep it looking its best.

Brush several times per week to prevent tangles and mats.  Professional grooming every 6-8 weeks for shaping and trimming.  Regular beard cleaning to prevent debris buildup.  Trim nails and check ears regularly.  Regular dental care helps maintain oral health.
Kerry Blue Terriers are generally healthy, but like all breeds, they are prone to certain health conditions.

sections.section: Potential Issues in the Kerry Blue Terrier:
sections.content: Hip Dysplasia: A common concern in active breeds.  Skin Issues: Dermatitis and allergies are known to affect the breed.  Eye Conditions: Including cataracts and entropion (eyelid rolling inward).  Progressive Neuronal Abiotrophy (PNA): A rare neurological disorder.

Loyal and protective—excellent family watchdog.  Energetic and fun—great for active households.  Intelligent and trainable—excels in dog sports and obedience.  Hypoallergenic coat—low shedding, suitable for some allergy sufferers.

Requires regular, professional grooming.  High energy level—needs significant daily exercise.  Can be stubborn—best suited for experienced owners.  May be aggressive toward other dogs if not socialized properly.
